title: Remove tracked vite.config.js that shadows vite.config.ts
description: A compiled copy of vite.config.ts is committed AND git-tracked (verified via git ls-files: vite.config.js, vite.config.d.ts, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo all tracked). Vite resolves config files in order vite.config.js -> vite.config.mjs -> vite.config.ts, so `vite`, `vite build`, and `tauri dev` load the .js file and silently ignore edits to vite.config.ts. `npm run build` (tsc -b) re-emits the .js so the build path self-heals, but `npm run dev` alone uses the stale copy — a config edit diverges silently in dev. Root cause: tsconfig.node.json is composite with no noEmit, so tsc -b emits JS+DTS+tsbuildinfo into repo root; .gitignore lists these files but they were committed before being ignored.
evidence: .gitignore lists vite.config.d.ts / vite.config.js / tsbuildinfo — yet `git ls-files` reports all four as tracked; tsconfig.node.json sets "composite": true with no noEmit.
suggestion: git rm --cached vite.config.js vite.config.d.ts tsconfig.tsbuildinfo tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo; stop emitting by dropping composite/references and typechecking with tsc --noEmit.

title: Set a Content-Security-Policy instead of csp: null in tauri.conf.json
description: The webview ships with CSP fully disabled. Tauri's security model treats the CSP as core defense-in-depth: with csp null, any HTML/script injection into the webview (biTurbo renders arbitrary agent/user-authored memory content and ingested code chunks) executes with full access to Tauri IPC and plugin permissions — including the unscoped fs read/write grants in capabilities/default.json. No dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink exists today, so this is hardening rather than open RCE, but the blast radius of any future rendering bug is total.
suggestion: Define a strict CSP (default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' asset: data:) relying on Tauri's automatic nonce/hash injection.

title: Revoke unused over-granted fs/shell/process/updater capabilities
description: The only frontend plugin imports in src/ are plugin-dialog (Projects.tsx) and plugin-autostart (Settings.tsx); no plugin-fs/shell/process/updater usage anywhere in the webview (updater driven from Rust via UpdaterExt which needs no capability). fs:allow-read-text-file and fs:allow-write-text-file are granted WITHOUT scope objects, meaning the webview IPC surface can read/write arbitrary user-writable paths. Combined with csp:null this is pure attack surface with zero current functional benefit.
suggestion: Delete the fs/shell/process/updater permission entries (keep dialog, autostart, core:*), or add explicit scope objects.

title: Make ensure-sidecar-placeholder detect and refresh stale placeholder sidecars
description: The script writes the 11-byte text 'placeholder' but afterwards can never distinguish that placeholder from a real binary. If a build is interrupted between placeholder creation and the cargo/copy step, or a user follows docs/release.md troubleshooting before running a direct `tauri build`, the text file gets bundled as the biturbo-mcp externalBin and shipped — MCP tools then fail at spawn with cryptic exec-format/JSON errors. Nothing validates the bundled sidecar before packaging.
suggestion: Read existing file: if content equals 'placeholder' (or size below sanity threshold), rewrite and warn; add post-copy sanity check in build-sidecar.mjs.

title: Build the MCP sidecar in run-wsl-cuda.mjs rebuild path
description: rebuild() runs `npm run build`, drops only a text placeholder, then builds just `cargo build --bin biturbo`. The biturbo-mcp sidecar is never compiled nor staged next to target/release/biturbo — this optimized WSL CUDA flow produces an app whose MCP server is missing (or a stale placeholder), breaking all MCP tools. Secondary: needsRebuild() scans src/, index.html, package.json, vite/tailwind configs but not public/, so changed public assets never trigger a dist rebuild.
suggestion: Also build --bin biturbo-mcp and copy to target/release (or call build-sidecar.mjs); include public/ in the mtime scan.

title: Isolate MCP test harnesses from the production data directory
description: mcp-smoke-test.ts (npm run mcp:test), recall-eval.ts and seed-memories.ts spawn biturbo-mcp with no environment override, and biturbo_mcp.rs hardcodes dirs::data_dir()/com.biturbo.app — every test run creates/deletes projects and memories in the user's real store, the same SQLite DB the GUI has open. Cleanup is success-path-only: delete_project runs inside try{} before finally, so any failed assertion, timeout, or crash leaves orphaned smoke-*/eval projects polluting real data.
evidence: this.proc = spawn(bin, [], { stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });  // no env/data-dir isolation
suggestion: Support a BITURBO_DATA_DIR override in biturbo_mcp.rs, spawn harnesses with fresh mkdtemp dir, move cleanup into finally blocks.

title: Guard release.yml workflow_dispatch from tagging a branch name
description: tagName derives from github.ref_name. On a manual workflow_dispatch run (documented in docs/release.md as the way to test the pipeline), ref_name is the branch name (e.g. 'main'), so tauri-action tries to create a draft release tagged 'main' containing binaries whose embedded version matches nothing.
suggestion: Add a workflow_dispatch `tag` input validated against refs/tags/v*, or skip release upload unless github.ref starts with refs/tags/.

title: Purge committed tooling artifacts (.opencode dylibs, tsbuildinfo, session state)
description: git ls-files confirms ~9.4MB of tooling junk committed: seven ~896KB x86_64 macOS dylibs under .opencode/tmp/ plus a V8 node-compile-cache blob tree (useless on any other machine), the two tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo caches, vite.config.d.ts, and AI-tool state files (.omo/run-continuation/ses_*.json session continuation — potentially private conversation data, .cursor/hooks/state/*.json, .mavis/plans/*). Bloats every clone, creates spurious diffs/merge conflicts, leaks local tooling/session state. None covered by .gitignore.
evidence: du -k .opencode/tmp/.*.dylib → 7 × 896KB; git ls-files tracks .opencode/*, .omo/run-continuation/ses_*.json, .cursor/hooks/state/*.json, .mavis/plans/*, tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo, vite.config.d.ts.
suggestion: git rm -r --cached .opencode .omo .mavis .cursor '*.tsbuildinfo' vite.config.d.ts and add these patterns to .gitignore.

title: Pick one package manager — package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml are both tracked
description: Two independent dependency-resolution sources committed: package-lock.json (used by CI's npm ci) and pnpm-lock.yaml, alongside pnpm-workspace.yaml. Contributors who install with pnpm update only pnpm-lock.yaml; CI then installs a stale tree from package-lock.json (or fails once it drifts out of sync with package.json). The repo mixes manager idioms: bun-style trustedDependencies, 'pnpm mcp:build' comments, npm everywhere else.
evidence: git ls-files → package-lock.json AND pnpm-lock.yaml both tracked; ci.yml `run: npm ci`; package.json has "trustedDependencies".
suggestion: Standardize on npm end-to-end (delete pnpm files) or commit to pnpm and switch CI/scripts; document in README.

title: Enforce version sync across package.json, Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json
description: release.mjs reads only package.json and tags v<version>; it never verifies src-tauri/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, or tauri.conf.json. docs/release.md instructs manually bumping six files — miss one and the GitHub release ships v0.3.0 assets whose app self-reports the old tauri.conf.json version, so the updater endpoint keeps offering the same 'new' release forever and version checks lie. release.yml likewise never validates tag↔version agreement.
evidence:
const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync("package.json", "utf8"));
const tag = `v${version}`;  // no comparison with src-tauri manifests
suggestion: Before creating the tag, parse all four manifests and hard-fail on mismatch (or auto-sync them).

title: Add frontend test/lint infrastructure and enforce it in CI
description: Rust gets fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo test in CI, but the React 18/Zustand frontend has zero tests, zero linting, and no tooling installed (no vitest/eslint in devDependencies; no test/lint scripts). Frontend regressions — store logic, the entire api.ts invoke layer, view behavior — are caught only by TypeScript compilation. For an app whose product is trustworthy memory storage, the UI half ships with no safety net.
evidence: scripts: { dev, build, preview, typecheck, tauri*, mcp:*, recall:eval, release } — no test or lint entry; ci.yml frontend coverage is just `npm run build`.
suggestion: Add vitest + eslint with test/lint scripts wired into ci.yml; start with unit tests for lib/store and lib/api.

title: Compress the 4.9MB public/logo.png used as favicon
description: public/logo.png is 5,134,912 bytes and is referenced as the document favicon in index.html. Vite copies it verbatim into dist/, so every installer ships a 4.9MB file the webview downloads at startup to render a ~32×32 tab icon — roughly 25× larger than the actual app icon (196KB). Pure waste in bundle size, disk, and startup I/O.
evidence: stat(public/logo.png) = 5134912 bytes; index.html:5 <link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="/logo.png" />
suggestion: Generate a small favicon set (32/64px PNG or .ico, ≤50KB) and move full-resolution logo out of public/.

title: Drop nonexistent landing/ package from pnpm-workspace.yaml
description: The workspace declares a `landing` package but no landing/ directory exists anywhere in the repo. Depending on pnpm version this either fails install or silently no-ops; stale config that misleads contributors.
suggestion: Remove the - "landing" entry until the package exists.

title: Sync .biturboignore with .gitignore (missing src-tauri/binaries/)
description: .biturboignore says it was 'created from .gitignore on first ingest' but has drifted: .gitignore ignores src-tauri/binaries/ (sidecar placeholders and multi-MB biturbo-mcp binaries) while .biturboignore only excludes src-tauri/target/ and src-tauri/gen/. biTurbo's own ingest will chunk and embed binary sidecar files into semantic memory, polluting search results and wasting index space.
suggestion: Regenerate .biturboignore from current .gitignore; ideally derive it at ingest time instead of maintaining a frozen copy.

title: Typecheck scripts/*.ts harnesses in CI
description: Eight TypeScript dev harnesses execute via node --experimental-strip-types, which strips types without checking them. No tsconfig includes scripts/ (root includes only src; tsconfig.node.json only vite.config.ts) and CI never typechecks them, so type errors accumulate silently until a harness crashes mid-run.
suggestion: Add tsconfig.scripts.json (noEmit, include scripts) plus a typecheck:scripts npm script wired into ci.yml.

title: Cache cargo builds, parallelize smoke job, cancel superseded CI runs
description: Every CI run compiles the full Rust dependency tree from scratch — the rust job has no Swatinem/rust-cache (release.yml does, so the omission is inconsistent), and the mcp-smoke job uses needs: rust, serializing behind it and compiling everything again with no cache. No concurrency group, so pushed commits queue redundant full runs; no dependency-audit gate.
evidence:
jobs:
  rust:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest   ← no rust-cache step; mcp-smoke: `needs: rust`; no `concurrency:` block
suggestion: Add swatinem/rust-cache@v2 to both jobs, drop needs: rust, add concurrency with cancel-in-progress, consider scheduled audit job.

title: Self-host fonts instead of fetching Google Fonts at every launch
description: The local-first desktop app preconnects to and downloads Fraunces/Inter/JetBrains Mono from fonts.googleapis.com on every window load. Offline — a primary scenario for a local memory tool — brand fonts fail silently and fall back, shifting layout; online, every launch leaks a request to Google, contradicting the local-first privacy positioning.
suggestion: Vendor the three families as woff2 (fontsource packages or committed files), declare @font-face locally, drop external links.

title: Add LICENSE file promised by README badge and package.json license field
description: The README badge links to ./LICENSE and the footer says 'MIT.', but no LICENSE file exists in the repo (verified via git ls-files), and package.json has no license field. Without a license the code is 'all rights reserved' by default — contradicting the badge and legally blocking the reuse/forks the README invites.
suggestion: Commit the standard MIT LICENSE text and add "license": "MIT" to package.json.

title: Fix release docs: pipeline builds NSIS .exe, not .msi
description: docs/release.md's build table claims the Windows release artifact is a .msi installer, but release.yml passes --bundles nsis, producing NSIS setup .exe files. README's Windows section similarly points readers at bundle/msi paths. Anyone following the docs looks for the wrong artifact name.
evidence: | Windows x64 | `windows-latest` | `.msi` installer |   vs release.yml: args: "--bundles nsis"
suggestion: Update docs to say NSIS .exe, or add msi to the release bundles.

title: Replace unmaintained fs2 and drop tokio 'full' feature bloat
description: fs2 is flagged unmaintained in the RustSec advisory DB (recommended successor fs4 offers the same FileExt API used for the cross-process write lock in db.rs). Separately, tokio's features = ["full"] pulls every optional subsystem into both the GUI binary and the MCP sidecar when only a small subset is needed — slower clean builds and larger binaries.
suggestion: Migrate db.rs to fs4 (drop-in FileExt), narrow tokio to features actually used (rt-multi-thread, macros, sync, time).
